clue.text: They bring us round fish Sarah found among others

indicators.note: found among says one group of letters sits inside another group here

parts.note: the others are other fish, smelts, carrying on the fishy theme of the clue
the ling is a long-bodied sea fish
Sal is a short form of the name Sarah

explanation.surface: A list of fish Sarah came across among the rest of the catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'others' is a loose pointer: after one fish (LING) the setter wants other fish, SMELTS, to hold LING and SAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Smelling salts are a pungent restorative held under the nose to revive someone who has fainted.

clue.text: How do King Cole's players manage to collect ?

definitions.text: How do King Cole's players manage

explanation.surface: A question about how Old King Cole's musicians get by, or gather things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Old King Cole's fiddlers three bow their strings in unison; and to gather something with difficulty from scattered sources.

clue.text: Topping metal-joiner, this churchman

indicators.note: Topping means cutting off the top, the first letter

parts.note: a welder fuses pieces of metal together

explanation.surface: A first-rate welder who also serves the church.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a lay officer in Presbyterian and other churches.

clue.text: Craftsmen causing mirth in centre of Piccadilly Circus ?

definitions.text: causing mirth in centre of Piccadilly Circus ?

explanation.surface: Skilled workers making people laugh in the heart of London's West End.
explanation.walkthrough: The statue at the centre of Piccadilly Circus, a London landmark, is popularly called Eros, god of love; the proverb runs 'Love laughs at locksmiths'.
explanation.definitionFit: Craftsmen who make and mend locks; and, by the proverb, those who amuse Love, the Eros statue.

clue.text: Point to a single tail-less bird in Africa

definitions.note: the definition names a place found in that continent

parts.note: N is north, a point of the compass
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: tail-less means the last letter is removed

parts.note: the robin is a small red-breasted songbird

explanation.surface: Directions to a lone bird missing its tail somewhere in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya, in East Africa.

clue.text: Those one " Sir "s, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of the quoted words may be put another way

explanation.surface: People whom one addresses as Sir.
explanation.definitionFit: Elders and superiors are the people one respectfully calls Sir.

clue.text: Sentence for one taking it ?

parts.note: a murderer takes someone's existence and is jailed for the rest of theirs: the punishment matches the crime

explanation.surface: What punishment awaits someone who takes it?
explanation.definitionFit: A prison term for the rest of one's days, the usual sentence for murder.

clue.text: Junction Eight's apt to be awkward

indicators.note: to be awkward means these letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: the s of the possessive is used as a letter

explanation.surface: Junction Eight of a motorway is likely to be tricky to drive.
explanation.walkthrough: Spaghetti Junction is the nickname of a notoriously tangled motorway interchange in Birmingham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangled multi-level road interchange is nicknamed after the pasta its looping lanes resemble.

clue.text: Where this puzzle is dated

parts.note: the crossword sits on a back page of the newspaper, and the same words mean old-fashioned

explanation.surface: Where the date sits on this crossword, or a complaint that it is old hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of date or old-fashioned; and literally located after the newspaper's title.

clue.text: Price cut has press chief in uproar

indicators.note: in places the newspaper boss inside the word for the uproar

parts.note: a ruction is a noisy disturbance or row
ED is short for editor, the chief of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Prices are slashed and a newspaper boss is in a fury about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut in price is a markdown, a lowering of the cost.

clue.text: Light of Love, if losing one, unconvincing

indicators.note: losing tells us to drop something from the little word if

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a lame excuse is a feeble, unconvincing one

explanation.surface: A lover's glow fades, becoming half-hearted once one partner is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A flame is both a burning light and, as in 'old flame', a sweetheart or passion.

clue.text: Capital beauty judge

explanation.surface: A judge of a beauty contest held in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The French capital; and the Trojan prince of myth who judged which goddess was fairest, awarding the golden apple to Aphrodite.

clue.text: What's in the wind ? Officer ordered to conceal nothing

indicators.note: to conceal has the officer's letters hiding the nought inside them

parts.note: OBE stands for Officer of the Order of the British Empire
O looks like the figure nought, nothing

explanation.surface: Rumours are in the air: an officer has been told to keep something quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wind' is the woodwind section of an orchestra, not gossip in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed instrument found in an orchestra's woodwind section.

clue.text: Sound sleeper in US like Mrs Leonowens' boss

indicators.note: Sound tells us the word is heard rather than spelt as given

parts.note: Americans call a railway sleeper a tie

explanation.surface: Someone who sleeps soundly in America, like the employer of a famous governess.
explanation.walkthrough: Anna Leonowens was governess at the court of King Mongkut of Siam, the story behind The King and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Leonowens' employer was the King of Siam, now Thailand, so he was Siamese, today's adjective for that country.

clue.text: Be patient with the Chief Guide on tour

parts.note: to bear someone is to put up with them patiently
a leader is a chief or head

explanation.surface: Bear with the head guide while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: A bear-leader was the tutor who accompanied a rich young man on the Grand Tour of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear-leader was a travelling tutor, the escort of a young aristocrat abroad.

clue.text: Limits interim distribution

indicators.note: distribution means the letters of interim are dealt out in a new order

explanation.surface: Boundaries set for sharing out a temporary allocation.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are end points or boundaries, the limits of a line or route.

clue.text: Cut Fielder — or give him his job back

parts.note: to reap is to cut a crop
point is a fielding position in cricket, square of the batsman on the off side

explanation.surface: Drop the fielder from the side, or restore him to his place.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone to a post they held before is to name them to it again.

clue.text: We get fed up about such labour

indicators.note: about puts the word for fed up around the clue's opening word

parts.note: sated means full up, fed to the point of having had enough

explanation.surface: We become weary of this kind of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed up' looks like bored, but here it is literally full, SATED, wrapped round WE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweated labour is work done in harsh conditions for very low pay.

clue.text: Descriptive letter from ..Greece penned by Miss Darling, mostly

indicators.note: penned by means written inside, so the letter sits within the heroine's name
mostly drops the final letter of the name

parts.note: Grace Darling was the Victorian lighthouse keeper's daughter famed for a sea rescue
phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A vivid letter sent from Greece and written largely by a woman named Darling.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace Darling is a British folk heroine who helped rescue shipwreck survivors in 1838.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphic writing is vividly detailed and pictorial, so the word is a synonym for descriptive.

clue.text: Canute's first little wave, one that halts

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter

parts.note: a ripple is a small wave

explanation.surface: King Canute's first small wave, which stops at his command.
explanation.walkthrough: King Canute is the English king of legend who ordered the tide to turn back. 'Halts' is the old sense of limps.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt is an old word for to limp, so a person who limps is meant.

clue.text: Dull surface, somewhat like a mountain lake?

parts.note: a tarn is a small lake in the mountains, a word common in northern England
the suffix -ish means somewhat or rather like

explanation.surface: A flat grey sheen of water, rather like a lake high in the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarnish is the dull film that forms on metal, a loss of shine on a surface.

clue.text: Picture about pasture-land is banned

indicators.note: about means the word for banned goes around the meadow

parts.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, forbidden
a lea is a meadow or grassland, an old poetic word

explanation.surface: A painting of grazing land has been prohibited.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a picturesque scene or living picture.

clue.text: This man makes payment in kind

annotationWithheld.why: This man makes payment in kind (4) for TYPE: 'kind' defines it, but no reading found for 'This man makes payment in'
annotationWithheld.clue: This man makes payment in kind

clue.text: Member of Muslim Brotherhood

indicators.note: of tells us the answer is made from a run of letters within the next words

explanation.surface: Someone who belongs to an Islamic political organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb, an arm or leg, is a member of the body.

clue.text: Express sorrow, having lost head with a bird

indicators.note: having lost head means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: to regret something is to say you are sorry about it

explanation.surface: Someone voices grief after losing their composure over a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The egret is a white heron, a wading bird.

clue.text: Anger erupts in a row

indicators.note: erupts means the letters burst out in a different order

explanation.surface: Anger boils over during a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a row' looks like a quarrel, matching the anger; it is a line of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a line or series, as in a mountain range.

clue.text: Will him to succeed

parts.note: read as a testament naming a man to inherit, rather than urging someone to do well

explanation.surface: Hope hard that he does well.
explanation.definitionFit: The person named in a testament to take over property or a title on someone's death.

clue.text: He can't return from (par -exemple) Elba

parts.note: ex is Latin for from, as in ex works
Elba is, for example, an island, which in French is an ile

explanation.surface: A man barred from going back from Elba, said with a French flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: The French 'par exemple' signals that Elba must be given as a French word: it is an example of an île. Napoleon was banished there.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone banished from their country is barred from going home.

clue.text: Boz was a false follower of Falstaff

parts.note: pseudo means sham or false
Nym is one of Falstaff's cronies in Shakespeare's plays

explanation.surface: Boz turns out to be a fake hanger-on of the fat knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Boz was the pen name Charles Dickens used for his early sketches.
explanation.definitionFit: Boz was Dickens's pen name, an invented name used in place of his own.

clue.text: Eighty-four pounds and seventy-five cents

explanation.surface: A weight and a sum of money set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundredweight is 112 pounds, so 84 pounds is that fraction of it; and in American money 75 cents is three coins worth 25 cents each.
